title: Russian grammar
intro: A working reference for beginners to intermediate learners. Russian shows a word's role with its ending (case), so most sections are about endings. Read a section, notice the shape, then listen for it in what you watch and read.

sections.title: Gender, no articles, and "to be"
sections.text: Russian has **no articles**: книга = a book / the book. In the present tense **"to be" is left out**: **Я студент** (I am a student); in writing a dash may stand for it: **Москва — столица России**. Words in **-ь** must be learned (день is masculine, ночь feminine). After **г, к, х, ж, ш, ч, щ** write **и**, not ы: книги.

sections.title: Present tense (two conjugations)
sections.text: Most **-ать / -ять** verbs follow читать (e-endings); most **-ить** verbs follow говорить (и-endings). Watch for consonant changes in the я form of 2nd-conjugation verbs: **любить → люблю, любишь; видеть → вижу, видишь**. Russian has one present tense for "I read" and "I'm reading".

sections.title: The six cases at a glance
sections.text: Every noun, adjective and pronoun changes its ending to show its role. Don't learn all tables at once: notice the question each case answers, and pick up endings from fixed phrases you hear again and again (в Москве, у меня, мне нравится).

sections.title: Accusative (direct object, direction)
sections.text: Only feminine nouns in -а/-я and masculine **living** beings change. **в / на + accusative** answers "where to?": **Я иду в магазин.** (compare prepositional "where?": **Я в магазине**).

examples.translation: Tomorrow we're going to the seaside.

sections.title: Prepositional (location, "about")
sections.rule: Most nouns take -е; feminine -ь and nouns in -ия / -ие take -и.
sections.text: **в** = in (inside, towns, countries); **на** = on, and also for open spaces, events and some places: **на работе, на улице, на концерте, на вокзале**. A few masculine nouns take stressed **-у**: **в лесу, в саду, на полу**.

sections.title: Genitive (of, absence, quantities)
sections.text: Uses: "of" (**машина брата**, my brother's car), **у + genitive** for having (**У меня есть кошка**), absence with **нет** (**У меня нет машины**), after **много, мало, сколько**, and after prepositions **из, от, до, без, для, около**. Numbers: **1 + nominative** (один час), **2–4 + genitive singular** (два часа), **5+ + genitive plural** (пять часов).

sections.title: Dative & instrumental
sections.text: Dative: the receiver (**Я звоню маме**), feelings and states (**Мне холодно**, I'm cold; **Мне нравится этот фильм**, I like this film), age (**Мне тридцать лет**), and after **к** and **по**. Instrumental: **с** = with (**чай с лимоном**), the tool (**писать ручкой**), and jobs after **работать / быть / стать**: **Она работает учителем.**

sections.title: Past tense
sections.rule: Infinitive stem + -л (he), -ла (she), -ло (it), -ли (plural); the ending follows the subject's gender.
sections.text: The past doesn't change for person, only for gender and number: a woman says **я читала**, a man **я читал**. A few irregulars: **идти → шёл, шла, шли; мочь → мог, могла; есть → ел, ела**.

examples.translation: Yesterday I was at the theatre.
We talked for a long time.

sections.title: Aspect: imperfective vs. perfective
sections.text: Most verbs come in pairs. The perfective has **no present**: its present-tense forms mean the future (**Я позвоню** = I'll call). The imperfective future uses **буду, будешь, будет… + infinitive**. Signal words: **часто, всегда, каждый день, долго** → imperfective; **уже, наконец, вдруг** → often perfective.

head: Imperfective
Perfective
rows: single completed result, 'did / will have done'
Я читал книгу. | I was reading / used to read the book.
Я прочитал книгу. | I read (finished) the book.
Я буду читать. | I'll be reading.
Я прочитаю. | I'll read it (finish it).

examples.translation: I read the news every day.

sections.title: Verbs of motion (идти / ходить, ехать / ездить)
sections.text: Russian distinguishes walking from travelling by transport, and one trip now from repeated or round trips. Prefixes add direction and make perfective verbs: **пойти** (set off), **прийти** (arrive on foot), **уйти** (leave), **приехать** (arrive by transport).

head: One way, now (unidirectional)
Round trips, habits (multidirectional)
rows: Я иду в магазин. | I'm going to the shop (now).
Я хожу в спортзал. | I go to the gym (regularly).

examples.translation: In summer we went (and came back) to the dacha.

sections.title: Adjectives & possessives
sections.text: Adjectives agree with the noun in gender, number and case. **свой** (one's own) replaces мой / его / её when the owner is the subject: **Он любит свою работу** (his own job).

sections.title: One-page memory map
points: No articles, and no 'to be' in the present: Я студент.
Endings show roles: subject, object, of, to, with, in.
в / на + accusative = where to; + prepositional = where.
у меня есть = I have; у меня нет + genitive = I don't have.
Мне нравится + the thing liked (in the nominative).
Past tense agrees with gender: я читал (man), я читала (woman).
Imperfective for process and habits; perfective for one finished result.
идти / ехать: one trip now; ходить / ездить: habits and round trips.
sections.tip: Listening strategy: unstressed о sounds like а (молоко → "malako"), so trust the stress. Catch the preposition and the word's last syllable together: в Москве, к маме, с другом tell you where, to whom and with whom.
